en: The water in the Banaue Rice Terraces changes from a liquid to a gas through evaporation under the hot Philippine sun.
Squeezing calamansi into water creates a homogeneous mixture called a solution where the citrus juice is the dissolved solute.
The colorful metal bodies of old Manila jeepneys undergo a chemical change called oxidation when they form reddish-brown rust.
Shaving a block of ice into fine flakes for a bowl of halo-halo is an example of a physical change.
Pumice stones formed during Mayon Volcano eruptions are solid rocks that float on water because they have lower density than liquids.
Floodwaters in the Cagayan River form a heterogeneous mixture called a suspension because heavy soil particles eventually settle at the bottom.
Baking dough in an oven to make fluffy pandesal causes a chemical change that produces new substances and cannot be reversed.
The hot springs in Tiwi, Albay release water vapor, which is water in its gaseous state, into the cool morning air.
When making salabat, ginger juice dissolves in hot water, demonstrating that some solid plant materials can form liquid solutions.
During the cold December nights in Baguio City, liquid water in outdoor containers undergoes a physical change to become solid ice.
Soaking raw fish in sukang Iloco to make kinilaw causes a chemical change that alters the protein structure without using heat.
Abaca fibers from the Bicol region have high tensile strength, making them an excellent solid material for manufacturing durable ship ropes.
